arguments: You are an independent source-grounded red-team reviewer. Use no tools. Output the requested JSON only.

attacks.title: Holiday-adjusted offer accepted by bare ordinal, then contradicted, qualified or stale follow-ups before the ledger write
attacks.assessment: I traced the A5 shape through the A6 source and found no path that writes 2026-11-02 after a bare-ordinal acceptance of 2026-10-27. When the phase is offer and nothing is missing, accept=True binds the bare day to the date of the current s.offer and rejects any other day (L127-129). The readback and the write both come from that same pending value (L50-56, L371-378). The residual risks sit elsewhere. (a) A month-first explicit date, such as 'November second', replaces the offer. For early band at now 2026-10-14 the deadline is 2026-11-02, so that date is valid. Only a correct producer row and the separate read-back confirm stand between it and the ledger. (b) The raw qualifier screen (L353) and the date screen (L83) are closed word lists. Words such as 'unless', 'though', 'provided' and 'hopefully' pass both. They are harmless only if the producer follows its contract ('qualified yes is proposal'). (c) In the confirm phase, an agree row with d (L369 requires no d) falls to L381, where phase!='offer' makes the bare ordinal raise 'missing month'. That is a safe over-rejection, but it can loop. (d) The except branch at L399-401 does not clear the stale s.offer. That is harmless today because the accept path is gated on the offer phase.
candidate_pointers: speech extraction_schema/0 description chunk C1 (elliptical ordinal rule, offer_context)
attacks.setup: now=2026-10-14T11:00 (Wednesday). get_account returns one personal_loan: past_due 360, instalment_amount 120, days_late 5. Early band: limit 1, deadline = 12th business day = 2026-11-02 (skips holiday 2026-10-26).
raw_turns: T2 DOB answer, T3 phone answer (verified)
T4 'Not today, but I can pay on Monday October twenty-sixth.'
Variant T5c 'The twenty-seventh, unless my salary is late.'
literal_event_rows: T5c conforming: k=proposal;c=1;d=the twenty-seventh;END ; forged: k=agree;c=1;d=the twenty-seventh;END
T5d k=agree;c=1;d=the twenty-seventh;END in phase confirm
attacks.producer_conformance: T4-T6 and T6b are advertised-grammar rows. The T5c agree row is forged or nonconforming extractor output, because the contract says a qualified yes is a proposal. user_raw is only an extracted copy.
attacks.failure_path: Expected correct trace for T4: L408-419 sees 2026-10-26 as not a business day and calls offer(360.0,'2026-10-27'), revision 2. For T5: L127-129 gives d=2026-10-27, and L388 inherits amount 360. readback() then sets revision 3, date 2026-10-27, phase confirm. For T6: L371 is valid, so vars.date=2026-10-27 and the route is create_promise. A failure exists only if the T6b, T5c or T5d variants reach create_promise with a date never read back. From source: T6b hits the 'instead' screen at L83, raises, and L399-401 goes to collect. T5c-forged passes L353 because 'unless' is not listed, so 2026-10-27 is read back and needs a later confirm. That is not a wrong-date write, but consent was qualified. T5d is safely rejected to collect.
attacks.expected_observable: The function_call_start body for create_promise contains date '2026-10-27' and amount 360, and the readback said '27 October 2026'. No body contains 2026-11-02 unless a later readback spoke 02 November 2026 and was confirmed.
positive_controls: T6 'yes, no problem' (confirm row) must produce exactly one create_promise with date 2026-10-27
Explicit 'November second' as a fresh proposal must be read back as 02 November 2026 before any write
attacks.witness_plan: Hosted chat using the call variables above. Read route_evaluated.variable_table for state.offer, pending and readback at every turn, then the create_promise args.body, then the ledger. Repeat T5 with 'the twenty-sixth' to exercise the 'conflicting acceptance day' rejection.
attacks.claim_limit: This is a source trace only. It does not claim A6 reproduces the A5 failure. Producer behaviour on T5c is unverified.

attacks.title: Partial-component retention without amount grammar, plus multi-row ordering using events[0] before filtering
attacks.assessment: The partial branch (L356-368) writes p['amount']=float(e['a']) with no amount-grammar check. Unlike L385, the decode value regex accepts 'nan', 'inf' and '1e2'. A 'nan' amount survives completion: every comparison at L408-415 is False, so the call reaches readback, and the L374 write guard then raises. The outer except routes to safe_failure. close_call is then sent with the stale vars outcome no_promise/service_error, which was set at verification (L192). That is a wrong outcome rather than a refusal or retry. '1e2' becomes 100.0 and could be recorded after a readback that speaks '100.0'. Separately, the partial branch mutates s['pending'] in place and clears the offer, while the vague and too_much branches leave pending holding stale dates. The support-phase check (L341-343) uses events[0] before the multi-row reduction at L344-347. With rows [refuse, agree] it closes as hardship. With rows [agree(no a/d), refuse] it transfers to support.

Variant T4n: same utterance, but the producer emits a non-numeric a
Variant (support phase) T7 'No, but okay, transfer me.'

attacks.producer_conformance: T4 and T5 are conforming. 'a=nan' and 'a=1e2' violate the 'explicit decimal amount' contract but pass decode, so they count as forged extractor output. T7 is grammar-conforming multi-row.
attacks.failure_path: T4: pending gets date 2026-10-29 with missing [amount]. T5: L386 sets 150, L420 runs readback() with the warning 'rest stays overdue', and confirm then writes. That is correct. T4n: pending.amount becomes NaN, readback says 'nan', confirm reaches L374 and raises, then safe_failure closes with no_promise/service_error and nothing is recorded. T7 in support phase: e=events[0]=refuse, so L343 calls finish(no_promise, hardship) and the agree row is ignored.

Single-row support acceptance k=agree;c=1;END gives transfer_to_agent support

attacks.title: Unfinished (c=0) safety intents gain authority through kinds membership; transport failure is not tied to a receipt
attacks.assessment: kinds is built from every row regardless of c (L265). The deceased, wrong_number, third_party, restructure and human checks (L271-279) and the hardship check (L339) never check c=='1'. A conforming truncated row such as 'k=restructure;c=0;u=unknown;END' transfers to restructuring, and 'k=deceased;c=0;u=unknown;END' closes as deceased. This contradicts the contract's own 'complete primary ... intents prevail'. Second, a create_promise HTTP 500 or timeout increments create_promise_failure_count and routes straight to safe_failure. The one retry required by rule 37 never happens, and the close is service_error even if the server recorded the promise (a delayed same-operation receipt). The 'signal must equal awaiting' check at L185 only binds the tool name, not the operation instance or revision. The identity and write gates otherwise hold.
attacks.setup: Verified customer in phase offer, same product.
raw_turns: T4 'Could we talk about lower instal—'
T4b 'My father just di— sorry, no, never mind.'
Write variant: T6 'yes, no problem', and the mock returns 500 or times out after recording
attacks.producer_conformance: All rows are advertised-grammar rows. c=0 with u passes the L157 check. The 500 case is a real API outcome documented in the openapi spec.
attacks.failure_path: restructure c=0: L276 calls transfer('restructuring') with no completion check. hardship c=0: L339 offers support and skips persuasion. deceased c=0 on a verified customer: finish(not_reached, deceased). 500 on write: failure_count>0 leads to safe_failure and close_call no_promise/service_error with no retry. A timeout where the server recorded leaves a ledger promise that disagrees with the close outcome.
attacks.expected_observable: transfer_to_agent queue=restructuring or close_call deceased after an unfinished utterance. For the 500 case, a single create_promise attempt followed by close_call service_error.
positive_controls: ok:false (HTTP 200) must retry once at L226-227
attacks.witness_plan: Run hosted chat with fixed rows. Compare route_evaluated with the variable_table event before the controller runs. For the write case, use only the hosted mock's naturally occurring failures and read the ledger plus the function_call_complete status.
attacks.claim_limit: Whether the producer emits c=0 for truncated safety intents is not observed. Whether the mock produces 500 or timeouts on demand is not established.

architectural_proposals: P1: Add a completion gate for primary intents. Act on deceased, wrong_number, restructure, human, hardship and stop only when c=='1'. A c=0 safety row should trigger one scoped clarification question, and an unfinished row must never gain authority by kind membership alone.

P2: Use one validated amount and date path. Route partial-branch amounts through the same regex and finite check used at L385 (reject nan, inf and exponents). Clear pending on every new offer or readback. Bind acceptance and confirm to an explicit {revision, amount, date} tuple, and reduce multi-row events before any branch reads events[0].

P3: Bind writes to receipts. Give create_promise an operation id (revision) stored in state. Treat an HTTP failure count as a controller signal rather than a static safe_failure edge, so the single rule-37 retry and the correct close happen. Reject a receipt whose revision does not match the authorized one.

guard_assessments.identity: Sound. get_account runs only after all_verified (L190-191) and is checked again at L210. The raw DOB fallback relies on an extracted copy but still requires the verify_identity service.
guard_assessments.write_binding: Mostly sound. The vars amount and date come from the readback, which matches pending (L371-378), and the write guard rechecks floor, deadline and business day. Gaps: NaN reaches safe_failure, and receipts are bound by tool name only.
guard_assessments.ephemeral_clears: event, user_raw, signal and api_result are cleared on every save or exception (L171, L183, L445). Stale s.offer persists after the date-error branch, and pending persists across offers.
guard_assessments.safety_precedence: Ordering is correct for complete intents, and hardship is placed before restructure. Completion is not checked, so c=0 rows act with full authority (P0).
guard_assessments.refusal_state: Attempts and limit are tracked. too_much converts to refuse after the floor offer. The support-phase decision uses events[0] before multi-row reduction, so the outcome depends on row order.

limitations: Source review only. Nothing was executed and no hosted results were available.
Extractor and producer behaviour is assumed, not observed. Platform behaviour on HTTP 500, timeouts and post-hook failure is not documented.
builder-checks are advisory and were not treated as proof.
No A6 source path reproducing the A5 2026-11-02 ledger write was found. The A6-01 negative result is limited by unknown producer conformance.

independent_qualifications.qualification: Offered Oct27 bare and month-first ordinal acceptance retains exactly 240/2026-10-27 after an earlier vague answer; subsequent consent prepares Oct27. No A5 Nov2 substitution reproduced. Explicit contradictory day/weekday and stale revision are rejected. Confirm-phase repeated ordinal safely re-asks. Native d=November second instead is not conforming complete date grammar; canonical d=November second with raw instead gives fresh Nov2 readback.

Conforming partial facts/latest amounts converge across both completion orders. Same-target multi-row facts and conflicting support rows are syntax-valid but producer advertises independently scoped product clauses; semantic conformance is ambiguous. NaN/inf/exponent tests explicitly violate advertised decimal grammar. Actual NaN confirm re-reads nan because NaN never equals pending NaN; it does not reach the write guard/safe_failure path claimed by Opus. Infinity is rejected by range; exponent 1.5e2 becomes 150 and needs exact readback plus later consent.

Incomplete kinds acquire priority from membership before completion (restructure/deceased/hardship/stop reproduced). Static failure-counter edge bypasses retry if that counter increments; no hosted HTTP-counter mapping or hook ordering was tested. OpenAPI500 explicitly says nothing recorded, so the native 500-after-recording claim contradicts its contract. Timeout-after-recording is separate and unverified. Same-operation stale failure replay cannot be distinguished by operation-name binding, but real duplicate delivery is unobserved.

independent_qualifications.architectural_qualification: Do not blindly clear pending at every readback: current write gate requires readback/pending equality, and clearing valid facts would break it. Replace obsolete offer/pending components by revision while preserving independent complete facts. Request IDs must be bound by actual transport/hook context; a self-declared client revision is not receipt authenticity.

independent_qualifications.recipient_followup: Saved real B10 confirm-kind/full-name failure is now independently verified; A6 also rejects this pattern under its own delimiter grammar and has no whole-bound-name fallback. Correct recipient kind and bare-yes decode-failure fallback progress only to DOB, never verification. Wrong/third-party/unfinished name controls remain unverified. Native Opus response preceded this fresh hosted steering; recipient conclusions are independent CPU/source followup, not additional native inference.

generic_recommendations.fix: Represent recipient assent separately from financial agree/confirm, make phase-specific kinds explicit, and use a narrow whole bound-current-name fallback even for a decoded phase-inapplicable kind. Exclude wrong-person/third-party/negated/unfinished mentions; advance only to security question, never set verified from a name.

Gate authoritative primary intents on completion and resolve all scoped rows before priority decisions; clarify unfinished or conflicting intent without creating transfer/closure authority from kind membership.

Use one finite decimal amount validator for partial and complete paths. Preserve latest completed sibling facts and explicit missing-component obligations; bind inherited offered day only to current complete offer and revision. Keep separate readback/consent.

Qualification-gate action-error routing and post-hook sequencing, then route eligible documented no-record failures through one controlled retry. Rebind each request body from immutable authorized terms and bind completions to request instances using verified transport context; do not add unsupported bank fields/endpoints.

judge.reason: The agent failed to progress the conversation after the customer successfully identified themselves. In messages 1 and 3, the customer provided the scripted name 'Sofia Almeida', but the agent failed to acknowledge this, repeated the request, and then ended the call without performing the required security checks (Date of Birth and Phone Number). As a result, no debt disclosure or promise creation occurred, and the ledger shows the incorrect outcome 'not_reached'.

existing_hosted_B10_recipient_evidence.qualification: Faithful typed name and extracted raw are identical in this case; failure is phase/kind mismatch, not an observed audio corruption. A6 delimiter-adapted CPU witness reproduces recipient rejection, but actual A6 extraction/hosted outcome is not known. No frequency claim about other first-ten cases or actor-induced partial loops.
